The learned Advocate further submits that in the instant case there is no eye witness and the alleged dying declaration on which the learned trial Court relied are not admissible in evidence and the learned trial Court failed to apply its judicial mind regarding dying declaration that PW.11 Sayer Ahmed I.O. stated in his cross examination that; মৃত্যুকালীন জবানবন্দি দেওয়ার সময় ডাক্তার ফয়জুল বারী উপস্থিত ছিলেন। আমি জবানবন্দি রেকর্ড করিয়াছি  but Dr. Md. Foizul Bari was not examined by the prosecution and who is the important witness. This witness has been withheld by the prosecution and presumption is, if had been produced in Court he would not have supported the prosecution and the decisions relied are not applicable in the instant case and in such a case the accused appellant is entitled to a benefit of doubt and the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence is liable to be set aside. 

 15. The learned Advocate in course of his submission submits that P. W. 2, 3. and 11 are declared hostile. The learned Advocate appearing for the appellant in support of his contention refers the case of the State -Vs-Laxmam Kumar and others reported in AIR, 1986 (SC) Page -250 where their Lordships of the Supreme Court of India held that "Declaration recorded by investigating officer- Time and signature of deponent absent- Capability of declarant to make declaration, doubtful held, declaration cannot be accepted". The learned Advocate for the Appellant further refers the case of State-Vs- Tota Mia and others reported in 3 MLR (HC) where their Lordships held "Dying declaration of a deceased as to the cause of his death is relevant under section 32(1) of the Evidence Act, 1872. It is a piece of evidence like other evidence which are equally subject to scrutiny by the court. Unless the dying declaration as compared to other evidence appears to be true. It can not by itself form the basis of conviction of the accused." The learned Advocate for the Appellant also refers the case of OMAR ALI -Vs- THE STATE reported in P.L.D. 1962 Dhaka Page-418 where a Division Bench of the High Court, Dhaka held that Dying declaration Weight to be attached depends upon circumstances in which statement was made, and authenticity of record Exact words not taken down Declaration unreliable Acceptance or rejection in pail, whether permissible." The learned Advocate for the appellant in support of his contention also refers the case of ABDUR RASHID Vs-THE STATE reported in P.L.D. 1966 Page-400 where their Lordships held that "Dying declaration Can be sole basis of conviction-Mere fact, however, that statement clear as to name and identity of assailant Does not make such declaration unimpeachable Murder Evidence of sole eye-witness disbelieved, statements of witnesses, as regards contents of dying declaration, bristling with material discrepancies; possibility that deceased, at time of making declaration, was prone to imagination and hallucination Basing conviction solely on dying declaration in circumstances, of case, held, unsafe". The learned Advocate for the appellant in course of his submission further refers the case of Alkas Mia and others -Vs- the State reported in 25 D.L.R. (HC) Page-398 where their Lordships held "Non-examination of independent witnesses particularly some of the neighbours, raises a presumption against the prosecution to the effect that had they been examined, they would not have supported the prosecution case"
